item.title: Iran declares Strait of Hormuz open to all ships during ceasefire
item.description: Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi declared the Strait of Hormuz "completely open" to all commercial vessels on Friday, linking the move to the 10-day ceasefire between Israel and Lebanon that took effect at midnight local time. The announcement marks the first time since the war began on February 28 that Tehran has offered unrestricted commercial passage through the waterway.

item.title: Pope Leo XIV draws massive crowd at Douala Mass
item.description:
Pope Leo XIV celebrated Mass before a crowd expected to number 600,000 at Japoma Stadium in Douala, Cameroon, on Friday, marking the largest gathering of his 11-day apostolic journey across Africa. The Vatican had predicted the turnout would be the biggest of the tour, though reports from the ground suggested attendance may have fallen short of projections due to extreme heat and tight security.

The liturgy in Cameroon's economic capital came on the pontiff's third day in the country, part of a broader April 13–23 tour that began in Algeria and will continue to Angola and Equatorial Guinea. It is the first time an American pope has visited the African continent.

item.title: US delays weapons deliveries to European allies as Iran war strains stockpiles
item.description:
The United States has informed several European allies that previously contracted weapons deliveries will likely be delayed as the war with Iran continues to deplete American military stockpiles, Reuters reported on Wednesday, citing five sources familiar with the matter.

Countries in the Baltic region and Scandinavia — some of which share a border with Russia — are among those affected, with delays hitting systems purchased under the Foreign Military Sales program that have not yet been delivered. U.S. officials communicated the expected postponements in bilateral messages to European counterparts in recent days, the sources said.

item.title: Oil plunges as Iran opens Strait of Hormuz to shipping
item.description:
Oil prices tumbled sharply on Friday after Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi declared the Strait of Hormuz "completely open" to all commercial vessels for the duration of the ceasefire between Israel and Lebanon, sending crude to its lowest levels in five weeks and fueling a broad rally on Wall Street.

Brent crude fell roughly 10%, while U.S. West Texas Intermediate also dropped by double digits, according to CNN. The sell-off marked the steepest single-day decline since early April, when the initial U.S.-Iran ceasefire announcement sent prices plunging more than 15%.

item.title: Trump keeps naval blockade despite Iran reopening Hormuz
item.description: President Trump declared on Friday that the U.S. naval blockade on Iran will remain in place even after Tehran announced it was reopening the Strait of Hormuz to international shipping, setting up a tense final stretch of negotiations before the ceasefire expires on April 22.

item.title: Iran war reshapes global energy policy as nations fast-track renewables
item.description:
The escalating conflict between the United States, Israel, and Iran — now in its seventh week — is reshaping global energy policy, as countries exposed to the largest oil supply disruption in decades accelerate their pivot toward renewable power.

Iran's blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, through which roughly 20% of the world's oil and gas supply transits, has locked an estimated 13 million barrels of oil per day out of global markets. A U.S. military blockade of Iranian ports, ordered by President Donald Trump on Monday after ceasefire talks collapsed, has further choked the waterway. The twin disruptions have pushed crude prices near historic highs and laid bare the vulnerabilities of fossil fuel dependency.

item.title: Trump says Iran agreed to indefinitely suspend nuclear program; Tehran denies it
item.description: President Donald Trump declared on Friday that Iran has agreed to suspend its nuclear program indefinitely, claiming a deal to end the war that has engulfed the Middle East since late February is "mostly complete." In a phone interview with Bloomberg, Trump said Tehran would not receive any frozen U.S. funds in exchange for the suspension and that talks toward a final agreement would likely resume over the weekend in Islamabad, Pakistan.

item.title: Iran reopens Strait of Hormuz amid ceasefire as jet fuel crisis grips Europe
item.description: Europe has roughly six weeks of jet fuel remaining, the head of the International Energy Agency warned on Thursday, raising the prospect of widespread flight cancellations just as the continent's peak summer travel season approaches. The warning came as the nearly seven-week closure of the Strait of Hormuz continues to choke off a critical supply route for global energy.

item.title: Breeding top 1-5% of corals could boost reef survival, study finds
item.description: A pair of studies published this week by an international team of coral scientists delivers both a warning and a roadmap: assisted evolution can help corals survive worsening marine heatwaves, but only if the research accelerates and selection is far more aggressive than anything tried so far.

item.title: Trump says Iran “agreed to everything” in war talks
item.description: President Trump declared on Friday that Iran has "agreed to everything" in negotiations to end the weeks-long war between the two nations, claiming Tehran will surrender its enriched uranium stockpile and indefinitely suspend its nuclear program. Iran has not confirmed any such agreement.

item.title: Trump says US will recover enriched uranium from Iran
item.description:
President Donald Trump said on Friday that the United States plans to work jointly with Iran to recover its stockpile of enriched uranium and transport it to the US, describing the effort as a gradual process that would begin soon.

"We're going to get it together. We're going to go in with Iran, at a nice leisurely pace, and go down and start excavating with big machinery… We'll bring it back to the United States," Trump told Reuters in a phone interview. He said what he called "nuclear dust" would be retrieved "very soon," referring to enriched uranium believed to remain underground after US and Israeli strikes on Iran's nuclear facilities at Fordow and Natanz in June 2025.

item.title: Trump says US has 'prohibited' Israel from bombing Lebanon
item.description:
President Donald Trump declared on Friday that the United States has banned Israel from conducting further airstrikes in Lebanon, issuing his strongest public directive yet to constrain Israeli military operations as a fragile 10-day ceasefire between the two countries enters its first full day.

"Israel will not be bombing Lebanon any longer. They are PROHIBITED from doing so by the USA. Enough is enough," Trump wrote on Truth Social. The statement came as part of a broader post in which Trump also pushed back against Iran's efforts to link the Lebanon truce to ongoing U.S.-Iran ceasefire negotiations. "This deal is in no way subject to Lebanon, either, but the USA will, separately, work with Lebanon, and deal with the Hezboolah situation in an appropriate manner," he wrote.

item.title: Iran denies agreeing to hand enriched uranium to US
item.description:
Iran's Foreign Ministry on Friday flatly denied President Trump's assertion that Tehran had agreed to hand over its stockpile of enriched uranium to the United States, exposing a sharp public rift in fragile nuclear negotiations between the two countries.

"Iran's enriched uranium is not going to be transferred anywhere," Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei told state television. He added that the "transfer of Iran's enriched uranium to the US has never been raised in negotiations".

The denial came hours after Trump told CBS News in a phone interview that Iran had "agreed to everything," including a joint operation to retrieve the country's roughly 2,000 kilograms of enriched uranium and bring it to American soil. "Our people, together with the Iranians, are going to work together to go get it. And then we'll take it to the United States," Trump said, adding that no U.S. troops would be involved.

item.title: UNICEF reports 172 children killed as Lebanon ceasefire takes effect
item.description: A 10-day ceasefire between Israel and Lebanon took effect at midnight local time on April 17, offering a fragile pause in hostilities after 46 days of renewed war that has killed more than 2,100 people and displaced over one million. As the guns fell quiet, UNICEF reported that at least 172 children had been killed and 661 injured since fighting resumed on March 2, with more than 415,000 children forced from their homes.

item.title: Pakistan deployed fighter jets to escort Iran delegation home from talks
item.description:
Pakistan's air force mounted a large-scale aerial operation to escort Iranian negotiators back from inconclusive peace talks in Islamabad, deploying around two dozen fighter jets and an airborne warning and control system after Iranian officials raised the possibility they could be targeted by Israel, Reuters reported exclusively on Friday.

The escort mission, which took place on Sunday following the collapse of the first round of US-Iran proximity talks, underscored the extreme security risks surrounding the highest-level engagement between Washington and Tehran since the 1979 Islamic Revolution.

item.title: Iran's buried Pickaxe Mountain site looms over nuclear talks
item.description: As the United States and Iran inch toward a possible deal ahead of the April 22 ceasefire deadline, a deeply buried nuclear facility near Natanz known as Pickaxe Mountain has emerged as one of the most contentious obstacles to any lasting agreement — and some analysts and Iran hawks are pressing President Trump to consider extreme measures to destroy it.

item.title: Iran threatens to reclose Strait of Hormuz if US blockade continues
item.description: Hours after declaring the Strait of Hormuz fully reopened to commercial shipping, Iran warned on Friday that it could shut the waterway again if the United States maintains its naval blockade of Iranian ports, escalating a standoff over one of the world's most vital energy corridors.

item.title: Israeli drone kills one in southern Lebanon hours into ceasefire
item.description:
An Israeli drone struck a motorcycle in southern Lebanon on Friday, killing one person on the first full day of a US-brokered 10-day ceasefire, even as President Trump declared on social media that Israel was "PROHIBITED" from bombing Lebanon.

Lebanon's state-run National News Agency reported that a motorcyclist was killed in the town of Kounine, in the Bint Jbeil district, after being targeted by an Israeli drone. The Lebanese army reported additional violations on Friday morning, including intermittent shelling of several southern villages and firing on an ambulance team in Kounine.

item.title: Israeli fire kills two UNICEF water truck drivers in Gaza
item.description: UNICEF said Friday it was "outraged" after two truck drivers it contracted to deliver clean water to families in the Gaza Strip were killed by Israeli fire at the Mansoura water filling point in northern Gaza. Two others were injured in the incident, which occurred during routine water trucking operations early Friday morning, according to the agency's statement.

item.title: Trump reverses course, renews Russian oil sanctions waiver
item.description:
The Trump administration on Friday issued a new month-long waiver allowing countries to purchase sanctioned Russian oil and petroleum products at sea, reversing its stated position just two days after Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Washington had no plans to do so.

The U.S. Treasury Department posted the license to its website late on April 17, permitting countries to buy Russian oil loaded on vessels as of that date through May 16. The license excludes transactions involving Iran, Cuba, and North Korea.
